GobyMeds Review 2026: Costs, Terms & Evidence

A source-checked look at GobyMeds' published pricing for compounded and branded GLP-1s, what the starter bundle includes, its 503A/503B pharmacy routing, HSA and FSA acceptance, and how its published cancellation and refund ladder actually works.

By the Clinic Scout Editorial Team · Updated 2026-08-06

Clinic Scout is independent and reader-supported — we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. It never changes a score. How we make money.

Bottom line

GobyMeds sells compounded GLP-1s as prepaid bundles rather than as a subscription: the compounded semaglutide starter is $299 for three months, which works out to $99 a month and includes the medication, shipping, the consultation and an injection kit. Its own terms say there is no recurring billing and no auto-renewal at all — one payment per order. The branded pens are on the menu too, at cash prices of $1,399 a month for Zepbound and $1,695 for Wegovy. The catch is what happens after you pay: a full refund is published only while clinical review has not yet begun, and once it has, GobyMeds may keep a $50 clinical-review fee — and the terms never say what becomes of the unused months of a prepaid bundle.23

Pricing breakdown

Compounded semaglutide starts at $99/month, sold as a $299 three-month starter bundle that includes medication, shipping, consultation and an injection kit; a single month is $169. Compounded tirzepatide starts at $133/month as a $399 three-month starter bundle; a single month is $299. The FDA-approved branded pens are sold at cash monthly prices: Zepbound $1,399/month and Wegovy $1,695/month.23

Eligibility and clinician review

Marketed as provider-reviewed care across all 50 U.S. states. The Terms of Service condition access on the participating provider being licensed where the patient is physically located at the time of care, and state that a residence, mailing, billing or shipping address does not by itself establish eligibility. No separate consultation fee and no membership fee up front — the consultation is stated as included in the bundle price. A $50 consultation/clinical-review fee (or another amount disclosed at checkout) may be charged or retained from a refund only if the patient cancels after clinical review has begun.1

Shipping

The provider does not publish a delivery timeframe.23

Cancellation and refunds

Cancellation is stage-dependent, requested through customer support, and effective only once GobyMeds (or the pharmacy/provider whose action is needed) confirms it. Before clinical review begins — and before any prescription, dispensing or shipment — the order is cancelled with a full refund. If a provider declines to prescribe, the order is fully refunded and no consultation fee is retained. If the patient cancels after clinical review has begun, GobyMeds may retain a $50 consultation/clinical-review fee. There is no subscription to cancel: billing is a single payment per order with no auto-renewal.1

Compounded-drug status

Compounded medications are dispensed by 503A or 503B pharmacy partners licensed in the patient's own state. GobyMeds states it does not operate a pharmacy or practice medicine: care is furnished by independent medical groups and prescriptions are dispensed by independent licensed pharmacies. Both compounded GLP-1s and FDA-approved branded pens are offered. Compounded drugs are not FDA approved and are not reviewed by FDA for safety, effectiveness, or quality before marketing.143

How to read GobyMeds pricing without inventing a total

The captured price evidence for GobyMeds is: “Programs start at $99/month; the compounded semaglutide starter is $299 for three months including medication, shipping, consultation and an injection kit” This review does not convert that wording into a recurring estimate when frequency, supply duration, inclusions, dose rules, or later-period pricing are absent. It also does not assume that consultation, laboratory work, supplies, shipping, membership, taxes, or follow-up are included. Each of those items is a separate verification question because combining them without direct evidence would create a price claim the source did not make. 1 2 3 4

A practical written quote should identify the first charge, every recurring charge, the billing cadence, the amount of product or service attached to each charge, the minimum commitment, renewal behavior, cancellation deadline, refund terms, and any charge that can change with dose or state. Keep a copy of that quote and the checkout terms. This is purchasing discipline, not a prediction that GobyMeds will impose any particular charge. 1 2 3 4

Eligibility, review, and fulfillment boundaries

The captured workflow language for GobyMeds is: “The provider does not publish a delivery timeframe.” This is not expanded into an end-to-end timeline unless the source defines the starting event and each stage. Intake completion, clinician review, prescription decision, pharmacy processing, carrier pickup, laboratory processing, manufacturing, and final delivery can describe different clocks. A single speed phrase cannot safely represent all of them, and no timeline establishes eligibility or an outcome. 1 2 3 4

Ask GobyMeds what event starts each clock, which stages can pause for records or payment, how status updates are delivered, and what remedy exists after delay, failed delivery, damaged goods, an unusable specimen, or a changed recommendation. Those questions are presented as a checklist, not as allegations that any failure has occurred. A clear answer should be retained in writing with the order or enrollment record. 1 2 3 4

Documented strengths and tradeoffs

Clinic Scout records strengths only when they arise from the captured page evidence or from the page's transparent handling of missing evidence. For GobyMeds, the documented positives are:

  • The bundle price is genuinely all-in: medication, shipping, consultation and injection kit are stated as included 1 2 3 4
  • The terms rule out subscriptions, auto-renewal and recurring billing entirely — each order is a single payment 1 2 3 4
  • HSA and FSA cards are accepted, and no consultation or membership fee is charged on top 1 2 3 4
  • Branded Zepbound and Wegovy are offered alongside the compounded menu, with cash prices published rather than hidden 1 2 3 4
  • Prescriptions are routed to a pharmacy partner licensed in the patient's own state, and the provider markets availability in all 50 states 1 2 3 4

These points do not become a star rating, medical-quality score, outcome measure, or endorsement. They describe what was comparatively useful in the inspected record. A source can be clear about one field and silent about another, so the review keeps field-level evidence separate instead of letting one visible term create a broad positive impression. 1 2 3 4

The same discipline applies to tradeoffs. For GobyMeds, the current record preserves:

  • The full refund is published only while clinical review has not yet begun; cancel after that and GobyMeds may keep a $50 clinical-review fee 1 2 3 4
  • The bundle is prepaid, and the terms do not say what happens to the unused months of a bundle you stop 1 2 3 4
  • No delivery timeframe and no LegitScript claim are published anywhere on the site 1 2 3 4
  • The pricing page still advertises a JUMPSTART20 promo whose own footnote expired on December 31st, 2025 1 2 3 4
  • Compounded drugs are not FDA approved 1 2 3 4

A limitation means that the cited record cannot support a stronger statement. It is not proof that the service is poor, unavailable, unsafe, or unsuitable. It is a prompt to verify the field directly and to compare the written answer with alternatives using the same standard. 1 2 3 4

A source-first verification sequence for GobyMeds

  1. Open each cited source and confirm that the relevant wording remains visible.
  2. Save the page date, URL, screenshots, and any checkout or intake terms that affect cost or eligibility.
  3. List every field that remains “not stated,” including cadence, supply, inclusions, timing, availability, and refund rules where applicable.
  4. Send those questions to GobyMeds and request answers in writing before payment.
  5. Compare the written response with the public wording and ask for clarification when they differ.
  6. Do not infer clinical quality, outcomes, or individual suitability from commercial transparency.

This sequence makes the review reproducible. Another reader can start with the same captured claims, inspect the same source notes, and see where a later page changed. It also keeps correction work precise: a correction should identify the statement, the current first-party source, and the date observed rather than replacing one unsupported claim with another. 1 2 3 4
